reflection.text:
High-dose imaging was dominated by huge cytoskeletal z-scores that anchored us wrongly: act_std z=+69.0 with nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 at 10 uM (e2) and tub_glcm_contrast z=+29.5 with act_std z=+24.5 at 1 uM (e6). I spent the 2-well budget on single rep-1 wells at 10 uM and 1 uM and then ran three dose_response tests (e10-e12) that were null with n=2, leaving no trend evidence. When review correctly flagged p=0.40 versus 0.30 as unjustified for Eg5, I flipped to Actin disruptors (p=0.52) because it had the largest z and the only direct visual call, but could not acquire the requested 0.1 uM onset well because budget was spent.

Unblinded as camptothecin (e17), the true DNA-replication/topoisomerase I mechanism was never in my hypothesis set, so cytotoxic clues like lower density and low cell counts (65 and 56 cells) were forced into spindle versus actin explanations instead of DNA-damage arrest followed by secondary rounding, compaction and actin clumping.

Recognized atlas uncertainty: initial Eg5 4/10 lead was weak and combined 3/10 vs 3/10 tie (e8) plus conflicting visual calls (e3 Actin only, e7 Microtubule stabilizers only) did not support confident Eg5 call.
Correctly flagged that dose_response e10-e12 with only 2 wells/doses added no trend support for mitotic fraction, tub_mean or rounding.
what_was_wrong: Mistook magnitude for mechanism: treated largest signal act_std z=+69.0 (e2) as proof of primary actin disruption rather than secondary cytoskeletal collapse from DNA damage/apoptosis.
Mistook tub_glcm_contrast z=+29.5 and rounding/mitotic-like features at 1 uM (e6) for primary spindle/Eg5 effect without any described monopolar spindles, ignoring DNA-damage-induced arrest as cause.

Excluded DNA replication/topo I from hypotheses and atlas interpretation, so late signal of Protein synthesis 3/10 and Protein degradation 2/10 (e14) was not used to reconsider non-cytoskeletal cytotoxic MoA.

Acquisition choice wasted budget: two single rep-1 high/mid-dose wells only, then failed to reserve a well for discriminating 0.1 uM onset phenotype that review requested to separate primary actin clumps from primary mitotic rounding.

Topoisomerase I inhibition traps cleavage complexes to cause DNA damage.

## Reflection

High-dose imaging was dominated by huge cytoskeletal z-scores that anchored us wrongly: act_std z=+69.0 with nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 at 10 uM (e2) and tub_glcm_contrast z=+29.5 with act_std z=+24.5 at 1 uM (e6). What was wrong or missed:
- Mistook magnitude for mechanism: treated largest signal act_std z=+69.0 (e2) as proof of primary actin disruption rather than secondary cytoskeletal collapse from DNA damage/apoptosis.
- Mistook tub_glcm_contrast z=+29.5 and rounding/mitotic-like features at 1 uM (e6) for primary spindle/Eg5 effect without any described monopolar spindles, ignoring DNA-damage-induced arrest as cause.
